Method of Attack: PowerDrop uses PowerShell and WMI (Windows Management Instrumentation) to create a persistent RAT (remote access trojan) on breached networks
Executed by WMI service encoded using Base64 to function as backdoor or RAT
Registers WMI event filters and consumers to trigger PowerShell script execution every 120 seconds
Sends hardcoded ICMP echo to C2 server as beacon
Decrypts commands from C2 using hardcoded 128-bit AES key and initialization vector
Executes decrypted commands and sends results back to C2 in encrypted chunks
Never touches disk as .ps1 script file, uses AES encrypted communications and ICMP protocol for stealth
Impacted Systems: networks of a defense contractor in the U.S.
Attack Vector: Possibly deployed via exploit, phishing emails, or spoofed software download sites
Executed via WMI event filters and consumers using wmic.exe command-line tool
